nodes.text: FAST · ON-DEVICE AI This document provides a summary of the United States Constitution. • Structure of Government : Establishes a bicameral legislature with the Senate and House of Representatives, where representatives are apportioned by population and senators serve six-year terms [1]. • Legislative Powers : All legislative power is vested in Congress; the President must sign bills passed by both chambers or return them with objections, after which they become law unless Congress adjourns during that period [2]. • President's Role : The Constitution defines the President as Commander-in-Chief and head of state with a four-year term, citizenship requirements, age limits, and a multi-stage electoral process for election [3]. • Federal vs. State Powers : States cannot levy duties on imports or exports without Congressional consent; all such revenues go to the federal Treasury under congressional control [2][3]. • Constitutional Provisions : The document mandates uniformity across the nation regarding taxes, commerce, currency, and naturalization laws; it also establishes authority over the militia, fortifications, and coinage [2]. • Impeachment Procedures : Impeachments must be tried by the Senate with exclusive authority to conduct them; conviction requires two-thirds approval of the Senate [1]. • Treason Definition : A person cannot be convicted of treason unless there is testimony from two witnesses or a confession in open court [4]. • State Relations and Entry : The Constitution mandates full faith and credit between states for public acts and records while citizens retain privileges across state lines [4]; new states must receive consent from existing legislative bodies to join the union [4].
